header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Time: 11:00 AM - 11:52 AM PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex M., Samir P., Priya D. (Redwood) / Nina G., Elliot P., Marisa C., Liam O' (PatientFirst)
summary: Customer requested confirmation on data handling: no-training-on-customer-data, retention policies for prompts/content, handling of PII/PHI, encryption/KMS, audit logs and SSO/RBAC. Redwood AE/SE reviewed SOC 2, VPC/private deployment options, and next steps for technical deep dive and documentation handoff.
transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this focused on security and privacy for the integration with PatientFirst. I'm Alex M., I'm the AE on the account. Samir (our SE) will run through the technical controls.
00:12 Nina (PatientFirst - Head of Security): Hi Alex, thanks. We have Elliot and Marisa from tech, and Liam from compliance. We're primarily worried about PHI/PII handling, and we need explicit guarantees about training \u2014 the legal team needs 'no training on customer data' confirmation.
00:28 Alex: Absolutely. Quick agenda: SOC 2 / ISO posture, SSO/RBAC, audit logging, KMS/encryption, data residency and prompt retention. Then we'll do Q&A and list action items. Sound good?
00:44 Elliot (CTO): Yep, sounds good. We have a couple of integrations planned; some user messages contain PHI. We want to understand how Redwood stores prompts and responses and whether anything leaks to model training.
01:02 Samir (Redwood SE): Quick callout \u2014 Redwood does not use customer prompts or content to retrain or improve base models unless you opt-in. For hosted customers we persist some telemetry for billing/metrics, but training pipelines are isolated and require explicit opt-in and contractual terms.
01:22 Liam (Compliance): Can you point me to the contractual language? We need an assurance that data is not used for model training, and also details of ephemeral vs persistent storage.
01:35 Alex: We'll send the specific clause. The short answer: no training on customer data by default, and we provide options for Dedicated and Private deployments where data never leaves your VPC. We'll include the clause in writing.
01:49 Marisa (Product): For hosted API, how long do you retain prompt logs? Our product analytics team needs some short-term traces for debugging, but compliance prefers minimal retention.
02:05 Samir: By default we retain request/response logs for 30 days for troubleshooting. We have configurable retention windows \u2014 you can set to 0 days, 7 days, 30 days, etc, depending on your plan and retention policy. For Dedicated/VPC, retention can be customer-controlled.
02:25 Nina: Do logs include full prompt text or redacted PII?
02:31 Samir: They include full prompt by default for hosted for up to retention window; however we have automatic redaction tooling and PII detectors that can be configured to mask or strip PHI/PII. For healthcare customers we recommend using our redaction preprocessor or host in Private.
02:49 Elliot: What's the redaction accuracy like? We're dealing with free-form notes, so false negatives are a concern.
02:55 Samir: It's not perfect; transcription and detection do miss some patterns. We can run a sample eval with your data (under NDA) and show hit rates, but for PHI we recommend Private deployment + customer-managed KMS to reduce risk.
03:15 Nina: OK. On encryption/KMS: do you support customer-managed keys? How are keys used for at-rest encryption and transport?
03:23 Samir: Yes \u2014 we support BYOK (bring-your-own-key) integrations with major cloud KMS providers. At-rest encryption uses envelope encryption; data keys are wrapped with the customer CMK. TLS for in-transit. For Private we also support HSM integrations.
03:40 Liam: Audit logging \u2014 we need immutable logs for access to secrets, model invocations that contain PHI, and admin actions. How granular are your logs and how long can they be retained?
03:52 Samir: Audit logs capture API calls, user auth events, admin changes, and KMS key operations. Logs are write-once and exportable to your logging endpoint (e.g., S3, Splunk). Retention is configurable; we can work with your retention policy. For Dedicated, logs are under your tenancy.
04:12 Marisa: What about RBAC and SSO? We want fine-grained roles so product engineers can't access PHI in logs, but platform ops can.
04:21 Alex: We support SSO (SAML/SCIM) and RBAC with role templates; you can map groups to roles. We also integrate with IdP for SCIM provisioning.
04:33 Nina: Do you support session recording or is that disabled for Private?
04:38 Samir: Session recording is optional and can be disabled. For Private, we default it off unless explicitly enabled.
04:45 Elliot: Could you talk about model variants and fallback? For example if we route to a cheaper model in low-cost mode, could that change outputs for PHI sanitization or hallucination risks?
05:00 Samir: Yes, model variants matter. We have model profiles and can pin a model for an endpoint; fallback is policy driven. We recommend pinning a consistent model for production cases involving PHI to avoid behavioral differences.
05:15 Nina: The legal team asked for a written \"no training\" guarantee and also a description of exactly what stored artifacts are retained.
05:23 Alex: We'll put that into an attestation and include retention tables. We'll provide SOC 2 Type II, and ISO summary if you need it.
05:34 Liam: SOC 2 report \u2014 can we get the full report or only a summary? Our procurement requires evidence of controls.
05:42 Alex: We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and a summary for general review. We'll send the NDA link and timeline.
05:50 Marisa: For the redaction preprocessor, is it synchronous? Does it add latency?
05:58 Samir: It's available as a pre-request hook. It does add small latency (~20-50ms per request depending on size), but you can do client-side redaction too. For high-throughput flows we recommend client-side or edge redaction.
06:15 Elliot: Data residency \u2014 we have EU patients; can you ensure data stays in eu-west regions?
06:21 Alex: Yes, we support region pinning for hosted; Dedicated offers region isolation. For Private, you control the region. We'll include region options in the doc.
06:33 Nina: One more on training: some vendors claim they don't train, but logs still flow into analytics pipelines. Can you explain how you segregate analytics from model training systems?
06:44 Samir: Sure. Analytics telemetry is aggregated metrics only, rolled up, and stored separate from model training pipelines. Training clusters are on a separate infrastructure and require strict access controls and a different approval process. No customer data is fed into training without explicit opt-in and documented mutual agreement.
07:05 Liam: What's your process if there's a suspected data exposure?
07:11 Alex: We have an incident response runbook \u2014 notify customers within 72 hours of detection, forensic analysis, remediation steps, and a post-incident report. For Dedicated/Private customers we can align incident cadence to contract SLAs.
07:24 Marisa: Do you produce replayable logs for debugging? That could include PHI \u2014 what controls exist?
07:31 Samir: Replay logs can be restricted \u2014 access is audited and requires elevated privileges. We can redact replay logs or provide sanitized versions for debugging. For high-security customers we recommend removing full-text prompts from replay artifacts.
07:49 Nina: Ok, can we get a security diagram showing network flows, where logs live, and KMS interactions?
07:55 Samir: Yes, I'll produce a VPC architecture diagram with envelope encryption flow and log export paths.
08:02 Elliot: Are there any known compliance gaps for healthcare (HIPAA) customers? Do you sign a BAA?
08:12 Alex: We are open to BAA discussions; our legal team handles that. Technically, we support the controls recommended for HIPAA \u2014 encryption, access controls, audit logging, and Private deployment options. We'll escalate to legal to confirm BAA terms.
08:29 Liam: Can we get a sample contract clause about 'no training on customer data'? We need precise language for legal review.
08:36 Alex: We'll draft an attestation clause and provide it.
08:40 Marisa: Can we get a short proof-of-concept in a Dedicated tenant to run a few transcripts through redaction and show metrics?
08:48 Priya (CSM): Yes, we can scope a short POC; we'll include the cost outline. We'll follow up to schedule.
08:55 Nina: For data retention, if we choose 7 days, are backups kept longer? We don't want hidden backups that retain data beyond that window.
09:05 Samir: Backups respect retention windows; persistent backups in Dedicated follow customer policy. For hosted, snapshots are rotated and subject to internal retention but not used for training; we'll include specifics in the packet.
09:20 Elliot: How do you handle deletion requests \u2014 e.g., GDPR right to be forgotten \u2014 if a user asks to remove interaction data?
09:27 Samir: We honor deletion requests; deletion is propagated through storage tiers. We can provide manifests of deleted objects per request. There is an asynchronous propagation window (up to 72 hours) depending on replication.
09:42 Nina: Ok that helps. For auditability, do you support exporting logs to customer-owned S3 buckets?
09:48 Samir: Yes, log export to S3, GCS, or to SIEM endpoints is supported.
09:54 Liam: We also want an immutable tamper-evident log. Do you support WORM or ledger-backed logs?
10:02 Samir: We support append-only logs and can integrate with third-party ledger solutions if necessary, or we can write to a WORM-enabled S3 bucket for tamper evidence.
10:12 Marisa: Any SLA on log delivery?
10:16 Alex: We can commit to near-real-time export for Dedicated customers; specifics in the SOW.
10:23 Nina: One last question \u2014 do you ever surface customer content in dashboards or training demos for your internal teams?
10:30 Alex: For hosted customers, internal dashboards show aggregated metrics only; we don't surface raw customer content in demos. For any demo with customer examples we'd request anonymized or synthetic samples. We'll include an explicit attestation on that.
10:47 Liam: Excellent. Can we also get clarity on who at Redwood has access to production data for support troubleshooting?
10:54 Samir: Access is role-based and limited; support access requires approval and is time-limited. We log and audit all support sessions.
11:04 Elliot: Are there any limitations to pinning models if we select dedicated capacity? Say we want an LLM with a particular quantization profile.
11:12 Samir: You can pin model versions and quantization profiles in Dedicated; some very exotic quantizations may need validation. We'll do compatibility checks as part of the POC.
11:25 Nina: OK thank you. Let's recap next steps.
11:28 Alex: Recap: we'll send SOC2 under NDA, provide the "no-training" attestation clause, share VPC/KMS diagram, schedule technical deep dive for encryption and logs, propose Dedicated POC and pricing. Priya will coordinate the POC schedule.
11:44 Marisa: Thanks everyone, appreciate the thoroughness.
11:47 Alex: Thanks all. We'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
11:52 [Meeting ends]

Notes: Some transcription errors present \u2014 speaker labels may be abbreviated. References to docs: SOC2 link (will be sent), VPC diagram (to be shared), redaction sample (can be provided under NDA).
